# Onboard Guide: Cabin Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Management

## Applies When
- Ambient cabin CO₂ partial pressure rises above 1000 ppm (approximately 3 mmHg).
- Crew experiences mild CO₂ toxicity signs: frontal headache, dyspnea on exertion, mental fog, or visual fullness.
- Primary environmental control and life support system (ECLSS) Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly (CDRA) telemetry flags degraded scrubbing efficiency.

## Action Steps
1. Verify localized air velocity and cabin ventilation: ensure inter-module ventilation (IMV) fans and personal diffuser ducts are unobstructed to prevent microgravity CO₂ pooling ("pocketing").
2. Check primary CDRA desiccant and zeolite adsorbent bed cycling telemetry on the environmental control panel.
3. Switch secondary ECLSS amine scrubbing bed or spare Amine Swingbed assembly from standby to active removal mode.
4. If exercising, temporarily reduce resistance workload or pause aerobic training until cabin CO₂ stabilizes below 800 ppm.
5. In sleep compartments, verify continuous airflow exhaust is operating to prevent localized breathing micro-bubbles.
6. Log serial cabin CO₂ readings at 30-minute intervals until levels decrease below nominal operational thresholds.

## Escalation Criteria
- Cabin CO₂ concentration surpasses 3000 ppm sustained, or spikes above 5000 ppm (contingency threshold).
- Severe throbbing headache, dizziness, visual disturbances, or cognitive confusion reported by any crew member.
- Failure of both primary CDRA and secondary backup carbon dioxide scrubbing systems.
- Don emergency breathing masks with independent O₂ supply, contact mission control ground console immediately, and prepare contingency lithium hydroxide (LiOH) canisters.
